article.title: Why Random Assignment Does Not Guarantee a Balanced Sample
article.why: Understand chance imbalance without confusing it with broken randomization.

paragraphs.en:
Random assignment is one of the strongest tools for estimating causal effects, but it is often misunderstood. People sometimes expect a randomized experiment to produce treatment and control groups that are perfectly balanced on every characteristic. Randomization does not guarantee that. It creates a fair assignment mechanism, while the realized sample can still contain differences by chance.

Imagine randomly assigning 1,000 customers to two groups. Even if every customer has exactly a 50 percent probability of entering treatment, one group might contain slightly more older customers, more high spenders, or more users of a particular payment method. These differences do not automatically mean that the randomization failed. Random processes naturally produce variation.

Sample size affects how large these imbalances tend to be. With very small groups, noticeable differences are common. With larger groups, major differences become less likely, although they never become impossible. This is one reason experiments with tiny samples can be difficult to interpret even when the assignment code is correct.

Teams should still inspect baseline balance. The purpose is not to demand identical groups but to detect implementation problems and understand the realized experiment. For example, if treatment customers were assigned before an eligibility filter while control customers were filtered afterward, a systematic imbalance could indicate a real design error. Unexpectedly extreme differences may also justify checking assignment code, exclusions, duplicate customers, or timing.

Statistical testing of every baseline variable can itself be misleading. With many variables, some will appear significant by chance. Conversely, with a small sample, an operationally important difference may not reach conventional statistical significance. Analysts can examine standardized differences, distributions, and business relevance rather than relying only on a collection of p-values.

Stratified or blocked randomization can improve balance on variables known in advance to be important. For example, customers can be stratified by company, rank, region, or prior spending band and randomized within each stratum. This does not guarantee perfect equality either, but it can reduce chance imbalance on key dimensions and improve precision.

The central idea is that randomization protects the assignment process, not the appearance of the final table. A balanced-looking nonrandom sample can still be biased, while a properly randomized sample can show some visible imbalance. When evaluating an experiment, ask first whether assignment was genuinely random and implemented consistently. Then inspect balance as a diagnostic, not as the definition of successful randomization.
paragraphs.zh:
Random assignment 是估計因果效果的重要工具，但常被誤解成 treatment/control 在所有屬性上一定完全平衡。其實 randomization 保證的是公平的 assignment mechanism，實際抽出的 sample 仍可能因偶然而不同。

例如1,000名顧客各有50%機率進 treatment，最後仍可能某組年長者、高消費者或特定支付方式使用者稍多。這不代表 randomization 一定失敗，而是隨機過程自然會產生 variation。

樣本越小，明顯 imbalance 越常見；樣本越大，大差異機率降低但不會歸零。因此仍應做 baseline balance check，但目的不是要求兩組完全相同，而是偵測 implementation problem 並理解實際 experiment。若 treatment 在 eligibility filter 前分組、control 卻在 filter 後處理，就可能形成真正的系統性問題。

對每個 baseline variable 都做 significance test 也可能誤導。變數多時自然會有一些偶然顯著；小樣本則可能有商業上重要但統計不顯著的差異。可搭配 standardized difference、distribution 與 business relevance。

對已知重要變數可使用 stratified/block randomization，例如按 company、rank、region 或 prior spending band 分層後再隨機。這不能保證完全相等，但能降低關鍵維度的偶然不平衡並提高 precision。

核心是 randomization 保護 assignment process，而不是保證最後表格看起來一模一樣。
paragraphs.ja:
Random assignmentは因果効果推定に強力ですが、treatment/controlが全属性で完全一致することを保証するわけではありません。保証するのは公平なassignment mechanismであり、実現sampleには偶然の差が残ります。

例えば1,000人を50％ずつrandomizeしても、一方に高齢者、高利用額顧客、特定payment利用者が少し多くなることがあります。これは直ちにrandomization failureではなく、random processのvariationです。

sample sizeが小さいほど大きなimbalanceは起きやすく、大きいほど減りますがゼロにはなりません。そのためbaseline balanceは確認します。ただし目的は完全一致の要求ではなく、implementation errorの検出と実現したexperimentの理解です。treatmentだけeligibility filter前に割り付けたようなsystematic differenceなら設計問題を疑います。

全baseline variableにp-valueを付けるだけでも不十分です。変数が多ければ偶然significantなものが出て、小sampleではbusiness上重要な差が有意にならないこともあります。standardized differenceやdistributionも確認します。

重要変数が事前に分かっていればstratified/block randomizationを使えます。company、rank、region、prior spending bandなどで層化し、その中でrandomizeすれば主要dimensionのchance imbalanceを抑え、precisionを改善できます。

randomizationが守るのは最終表の見た目ではなくassignment processです。balanceは成功条件そのものではなくdiagnosticとして扱います。

business.term: Randomization protects the assignment process, not perfect balance in the realized sample.
business.explanation: 解釋隨機分派與樣本平衡的核心差異。
